name: CHCKX Filament
summary: Amazon-first budget filament label with a WooCommerce storefront at chckx3d.com, spanning PLA and specialty PLA through engineering grades (ABS, PETG, PCTG, TPU, PA6-GF, PP-CF/PP-GF, PPA-CF) at prices three to four times below market for the engineering materials. The about page claims in-house vertically-integrated US production and ISO-certified quality control, but no certificate number, factory, plant photo or legal entity is given, and no TDS or SDS exists for any product. The stated headquarters, 1234 N Spring St, Los Angeles CA 90012, resolves to a residential condo unit per Redfin; the only contact is a personal Gmail address (yinchangfeng86@gmail.com); no social profiles exist; and one product page (PETG) still contains placeholder text reading "Test". The evidence therefore points to a reseller or rebrand of undisclosed third-party OEM production rather than a manufacturer. A Prusa community forum thread reports two products as materially mislabeled — a "PPS-CF" and a "PPA-CF" said to resemble PA6-CF — but re-verification on 2026-08-01 established these are user observations from side-by-side print comparisons, not instrumented lab analysis, and no second independent source repeats either claim (see provenance.conflicts). The same thread describes PC spools and thermally printed labels that smear. Treat all chemistry claims on this brand as unverified, and treat the mislabeling claims as unconfirmed suspicion rather than as findings.

oem_relationships.notes: No factory, plant, legal entity or ISO certificate number is disclosed anywhere on the site or in listings. The residential-condo headquarters address, personal Gmail contact, Amazon-first distribution, absence of any TDS/SDS, and engineering-grade pricing three to four times below market are all consistent with rebranded imported spools rather than in-house extrusion. China origin is inferred from the distribution and pricing pattern only; the actual producer is unidentified and the relationship is suspected, not confirmed.

product_lines.name: PPA-CF Filament
product_lines.notes: Sold as 10% carbon-fiber PPA at $22.79 with a claimed HDT of 195C and 280-310C nozzle / 100-120C bed. Chemistry is disputed but unresolved: one Prusa forum user reports the product is 'PA6-CF in disguise' after side-by-side Benchy prints against genuine Siraya Tech PPA-CF under identical drying (12 h at 85C), the CHCKX print coming out markedly inferior. Re-verified 2026-08-01: that report is a visual/print-quality comparison with no density, DSC or FTIR measurement behind it, and no second independent source repeats it. The ppa-cf id follows the vendor's labeling and is deliberately NOT reclassified to pa6-cf on this evidence — but the labeling should not be relied on either.

additional_notes: Origin is unresolved and manufacturing_countries is deliberately left empty. headquarters_country is set to United States because that is the storefront's claimed base (1234 N Spring St, Los Angeles CA 90012), but Redfin shows that address as a residential condo unit, not an industrial or warehouse site, so it is best read as a mail/registration address rather than a plant. No factory location, corporate entity, ISO certificate number, TDS or SDS was found anywhere, so the country where the filament is actually extruded cannot be asserted in either direction; China is a suspicion recorded under oem_relationships, not a finding. Distribution is primarily Amazon (ASINs B0FLK2KDSX, B0FLK15JP8, B0FLJXQH5D, B0FLK1NRN9), where 3dfilamentprofiles.com catalogs 150+ SKU/color combinations, a range far wider than the 14 SKUs on the company storefront. The Prusa forum thread additionally notes PC spools and thermally printed labels that smear in handling. Build plates: none found, so makes_plates is left unset. All quoted fiber loadings, HDT and modulus figures are vendor marketing claims with no supporting documentation.

provenance.conflicts: Identity is contested. The about page claims in-house, vertically integrated US manufacturing with ISO-certified quality control, but supplies no certificate number, factory, plant imagery or legal entity, and no TDS or SDS exists for any SKU. Against that claim: the stated Los Angeles headquarters resolves to a residential condo unit per Redfin, the only contact is a personal Gmail address, distribution is Amazon-first with a catalog several times larger than the storefront, no social presence exists, and one product page still carries placeholder text. Engineering-grade filaments are priced three to four times below market. The weight of evidence favours a reseller/rebrand of undisclosed third-party OEM production, likely China-based, over the claimed US manufacturer; neither is proven. Product labeling is separately contested, and re-verification on 2026-08-01 downgraded how that contest should be described — the claim is STILL OPEN and nothing was reclassified. The Prusa thread ('How to pick up CHCKX') was re-read directly and the PPA-CF claim is verbatim: user hyiger writes 'I did some more tests on the "PPA-CF" and I'm pretty sure it's PA6-CF in disguise... resemble[s] PA6-CF', based on side-by-side Benchy prints against genuine Siraya Tech PPA-CF after identical drying (12 h at 85C), with the CHCKX print described as 'garbage', off-color and printing 'dirty'. No density measurement, DSC, FTIR or other instrumented test was performed or cited, so this is a credible but non-instrumented community report, not the 'independent testing' this entry previously called it — that wording is corrected here and in summary/product_lines. No second independent source — a different user, a lab result, a reviewer — making the same PA6-CF claim could be found; the Bambu Lab forum thread on CHCKX PPS-CF pricing returned 403 on direct fetch and its search snippets carry general price/quality skepticism but no PPA-CF identity claim. It does sit in a broader pattern: the same thread separately suspects the 'PPS-CF' of being mislabeled commodity resin. Note a discrepancy this entry has not resolved — the re-read surfaced the PPS-CF suspicion as PP-CF argued from density reasoning, whereas the ABS-based characterisation recorded earlier in this entry was not reproduced; neither version is instrumented and both are recorded as unconfirmed. Confidence stays low. headquarters_country (claimed storefront base) and manufacturing_countries (left empty) should not be read as verified.
